newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Dengue fever claims 28 lives in Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Dengue fever claims 28 lives in Malaysia.

text.p: Dengue haemorrhagic fever has claimed 28 lives among 487 victims in Malaysia this year, but the outbreak is expected to peak in the next few weeks, the World Health Organisation (WHO) said on Friday.
The United Nations agency, in its weekly bulletin, also said that some 11,328 cases of dengue fever had been reported in the period to July 26. This form rarely causes death.
"Based on previous epidemiological patterns, it is expected that the outbreak will peak in the next few weeks," WHO said, based on a report from its collaborating centre in Kuala Lumpur.
The death rate from dengue haemorrhagic fever was 85.1 per cent higher than for the same period last year.

Dengue is a mosquito-borne infection, endemic in more than 100 countries, which has become a major international public health concern. It is a severe flu-like illness found in tropical regions, mainly in urban areas.

A more lethal complication, dengue haemorrhagic fever, is the leading cause of childhood death in many countries. It is characterised by high fever and bleeding, often with enlargement of the liver and circulatory failure in severe cases.
